title: 3Sum
statement: Return every unique triplet `[a, b, c]` in `nums` such that a + b + c = 0. The result must not contain duplicate triplets. Return the triplets sorted, and sort the list of triplets.
hints: Sort first. Duplicate values then sit together and can be skipped.
Fix one number and solve two-sum on the remainder with opposite pointers.
After recording a triplet, advance both pointers past copies of the values you just used.

approaches.name: Triple loop with a set
approaches.explanation: Enumerate triples and store canonical sorted tuples.

approaches.name: Sort plus two pointers
approaches.explanation: Fix the smallest element, then scan the rest inward. Output space is extra.

editorial: Sorting costs n log n and makes uniqueness local. For each index i, skip it when nums[i] equals nums[i-1]. Then run the sorted two-sum procedure on i+1 and the end, targeting -nums[i]. Each successful hit skips duplicate left and right values so the same triplet is not emitted again.
